summary: This bill creates a State Department-led interagency task force that must produce and carry out a strategy to shut down Southeast Asian scam compounds run by forced-labor trafficking victims, including by imposing sanctions on named individuals and groups, recovering stolen funds, and coordinating with foreign partners and U.S. agencies.

scores.thoughts: The bill authorizes $30 million in appropriations for the Department of State for FY 2026 and 2027 to implement the strategy and related programs. This represents a modest expansion of federal spending on a new interagency initiative.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax policy, or revenue measures.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare policy or systems.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms or gun regulations.
The bill addresses human trafficking victims in foreign scam compounds but does not alter U.S. immigration law, pathways, or border policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion or reproductive rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental regulations or climate policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to domestic welfare programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to education policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement or decriminalization.
The bill focuses on international criminal syndicates and sanctions rather than domestic criminal justice reform, sentencing, or policing.
The bill contains no provisions related to trade agreements or tariffs.
The bill authorizes limited new spending but does not address deficit reduction or debt policy.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ rights or protections.
The bill authorizes programs to build foreign law enforcement capacity and support trafficking victims abroad, representing a targeted form of foreign assistance.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access or election integrity.
The bill directs partnerships with tech companies and use of offensive cyber capabilities to disrupt scam operations, implying modest expansion of government-tech coordination.
The bill contains no provisions related to labor unions or worker protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious liberty or anti-discrimination law.
